messages:
sam_w: quick sync — we need a clear decision surface for QKV layout & kernel contracts (NHWC vs NCHW, packed QKV vs 3-tensor). perf numbers diverge and ops fusibility depends on layout. thinking we either standardize one internal canonical layout or expose packing as part of the model manifest. thoughts?
anya_k: +1 to a manifest flag. runtime can choose cheapest kernel but we need stable kernel entry signatures. otherwise kernel authors keep chasing variants. :thinking:
kevin_m: propose two orthogonal axes: memory_format (NHWC|NCHW) and qkv_packing (packed|separate). Kernel API should accept (memory_format, qkv_packing) and runtime picks kernel implementation. that keeps contract small.
julia_r: I like the axes but beware of copy cost when converting packing. for some LLM configs copying QKV into packed buffer is expensive for long contexts. we measured ~0.5-1.2ms for 512 seq on A100 when doing an extra pack step.
sam_w: noted. do we rely on kernel authors to implement both pack variants? or have a shared utility to do pack/unpack in runtime with fast vectorized paths?
kevin_m: shared util + 2 canonical kernel entrypoints IMO:
```
// kernel signatures
void mha_packed_qkv(float* packed_qkv, int b, int s, int h, int d_head, ...);
void mha_separate_qkv(float* Q, float* K, float* V, int b, int s, int h, int d_head, ...);
```
That keeps kernels simple and lets runtime convert when only one impl exists.
anya_k: +1 to two entrypoints. also we need stride/alignment guarantees in the contract: 64B/128B alignment for vector loads, contiguous head-major ordering for packed. otherwise performance cliff.
julia_r: can we add a tiny descriptor struct in the manifest (but not in kernel ABI) that states: stride_bytes, alignment, head_stride, element_size. runtime validates before invoking. cheap check.
sam_w: prefer no extra ABI payload — runtime can expose a normalized view to kernels. but metadata file in model manifest ok. we should ensure HWI (hardware info) influences padding suggestions.
kevin_m: note: NHWC (batch, seq, head, head_dim) wins for contiguous per-head matmul and fused attention kernels. NCHW sometimes better for op reuse with conv inference but less ideal for per-head reductions. empirically NHWC packed_qkv gave 8-12% lower latency on large BERT-like runs.
anya_k: quantized kernels (int8/4bit) change alignment needs: prefer multiples of 32 or 64 elements to use tensor cores / DPX-like ops. add that to kernel contract.
julia_r: practical suggestion: runtime attempts to call the best-fitting kernel signature. fallback order: exact-native-packed -> native-separated -> runtime-pack-then-packed. logs metrics when a copy path used. make it visible in Console.
kevin_m: encoding of manifest example:
```
model_manifest:
  memory_format: NHWC
  qkv_packing: packed
  preferred_alignment: 128
  fallback_packing: separate
```
That informs scheduling and placement decisions.
sam_w: operational concerns: adding two entrypoints per kernel increases maintenance surface but simplifies runtime. acceptable tradeoff?
anya_k: maintenance cost is fine. ops team can provide reference packed->separate helpers in C++/CUDA repo. publish microbenchmarks.
kevin_m: small gotcha: some older kernels assume contiguous batch-major layout; we must test with non-contiguous stride views (e.g., when KV caching slices). Kernel contracts should disallow arbitrary strides unless explicitly supported.
julia_r: agree. add automated lit tests for: unit stride, stride with head padding, and sliced-kv views.
infra-bot: deploy:perf-canary pipeline started for branch "qkv-contracts" — results expected in ~2h.
sam_w: next steps: (1) agree on axis names + enum values, (2) add two kernel entrypoints to runtime ABI, (3) implement fast runtime pack util, (4) add manifest fields + console surfaced copy metrics. I'll open an RFC PR with those points.
kevin_m: I'll stub kernel entrypoints and unit tests.
anya_k: I'll draft manifest schema and Console telemetry hooks.
julia_r: I'll run microbenchmarks for 32/128/512 seq and both INT8/FP16 to quantify copy break-even.
sam_w: thanks — ping here when canary results land. :white_check_mark:
